name: Outbound UI Decoupling and Presentation Surface Refactor
description: Move ephemeral UI ownership closer to the core by introducing a core/outbound presentation surface, shared presentation state, and unified handling for replaceable menus, status, and streaming across channels.

userStories.title: Define core presentation surface model in core/outbound
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a canonical presentation surface model in core/outbound so that channels stop inventing their own UI-state conventions.
acceptanceCriteria: A core-owned type or set of types defines reusable presentation concepts such as replaceable surfaces, slots, and update semantics.
The model lives under core/outbound and does not reference Telegram-, Discord-, or adapter-specific API names.
Existing outbound flows can map to the new model without changing visible behavior.
There is test coverage proving the model can represent reusable/editable UI independently of channel-specific mechanics.
userStories.notes:
Branch: us/us-001-core-presentation-surface
Status: complete
Files: src/donkey/core/outbound/outbound.nim; tests/core/t_outbound.nim
Tests: added coverage for replaceable surfaces, streaming surfaces, and projection into OutboundMessage
Validation: nim c --mm:orc -r tests/core/t_outbound.nim ✅; nim c --mm:orc src/donkey.nim ✅; nim c --mm:orc -r tests/adapters/channel/t_telegram_runtime.nim ✅; nim c --mm:orc -r tests/channel/t_discord.nim ✅; nim c --mm:orc -r tests/app/t_outbound_runtime.nim ✅; nim c --mm:orc -r tests/app/t_orchestrator.nim emitted all green test cases but the runner stayed alive after completion; nim c --mm:orc -r tests/adapters/channel/t_common_runtime.nim ✅
Risks: the shared presentation model is introduced but not yet consumed broadly outside existing outbound helpers.
Carry forward: core/outbound now owns PresentationSurface, PresentationMessage, replaceable vs streaming semantics, and projection into OutboundMessage.

userStories.title: Introduce presentation state boundary for replaceable menus
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want presentation state managed through a dedicated boundary so that adapters no longer own mutable UI slot bookkeeping directly for replaceable menus.
acceptanceCriteria: A runtime or port is introduced to manage presentation state such as slot-to-message bindings for replaceable menus.
Telegram and Discord no longer implement their own slot keying helpers locally.
The new boundary is reusable from multiple channel runtimes.
Existing bootstrap replacement behavior continues to work unchanged.

userStories.title: Migrate menu config models think and help to presentation runtime
userStories.description: As a user, I want interactive menus to behave consistently across channels so that opening one surface does not accidentally stomp another.
acceptanceCriteria: menu, config, models, think, and help use the shared presentation runtime instead of adapter-local state tables.
Telegram and Discord each preserve their current UX semantics where supported.
Separate UI surfaces keep independent state and do not overwrite each other accidentally.
Regression tests cover at least one multi-surface scenario per supported interactive channel.

userStories.title: Bring status and streaming into the same presentation model
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want status and streaming surfaces modeled in the same system so that ephemeral presentation behavior is not split across unrelated mechanisms.
acceptanceCriteria: The design explicitly covers status and streaming-related UI updates, not just static menus.
Existing stream and status tracking is migrated or wrapped so it fits the shared presentation model.
The implementation distinguishes reusable UI surfaces from append-only content where necessary.
There are tests showing that status and streaming flows do not regress while adopting the shared model.

userStories.title: Move fallback copy ownership into the presentation boundary
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want fallback copy for non-editable channels owned by the presentation boundary so that projection behavior stays generic and consistent.
acceptanceCriteria: The presentation boundary owns fallback copy and semantics for non-editable channels.
Channel runtimes project fallback UI without inventing their own wording for shared surfaces.
Presentation logic can ask whether a channel supports replacement, editing, components, or related capabilities without naming specific channels.
Adding a new channel requires wiring capabilities and projection only, not copying orchestration logic or fallback text policy.
userStories.notes: Open-question resolution: the shared boundary owns fallback copy.

userStories.title: Document and harden the presentation architecture
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the presentation model documented so that future UI work follows the same architectural direction instead of reintroducing adapter-local state.
acceptanceCriteria: The repo documents the presentation architecture and intended ownership boundaries.
The documentation explains where orchestration decisions belong versus where ports and adapters project them.
The documentation covers editable surfaces, non-editable fallbacks, slot or state ownership, and status or streaming surfaces.
At least one representative code path under core/outbound is referenced in the documentation.
